docs.title: OpenMembraneBuilder-v1.2.0-dev
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder is a graphical and command-line tool for building Martini coarse-grained membrane and membrane–protein systems.

It supports:

  • Membrane-only systems
  • Membrane systems with coarse-grained proteins
  • Martini v3 force fields
  • Reproducible JSON-based builds
  • GUI and CLI workflows
  • Automatic zipped output folders

docs.title: 🚀 Main Workflow
docs.text: GUI input → Config object → System build → config.json → ZIP archive

docs.title: 📁 Output Structure
docs.text:
Each build creates a self-contained project folder:

outputs/OpenMembraneBuilder-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS/
├── config.json
├── user_inputs/
├── simulations/
├── toppar/
└── mdp/

docs.title: 📦 Zipped Output
docs.text:
A compressed archive is also created automatically:

downloads/OpenMembraneBuilder-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.zip

This archive contains everything needed to reproduce the system, including:

  • Input files (user_inputs/)
  • Configuration (config.json)
  • Simulation setup files

docs.text: • https://github.com/lolicato/OpenMembraneBuilder

docs.title: Related Software
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder builds on several outstanding open-source scientific projects:

  • COBY
  • MDAnalysis
  • Streamlit
  • NumPy
  • SciPy

Please also cite these projects where appropriate.

docs.title: Future Publication
docs.text: A dedicated publication describing OpenMembraneBuilder is planned for future release.

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder can run without the GUI using a saved JSON configuration.

python app.py --no-gui config.json

docs.title: 🎯 Why use the CLI
docs.text:
The CLI mode is useful for:

  • Repeating a previous build
  • Quickly swapping proteins
  • Automating workflows
  • Running batch simulations

docs.title: 1. Create a configuration via GUI
docs.text:
streamlit run app.py

Build your system once. This generates a project folder with a config.json.

docs.title: 2. Re-run using CLI
docs.text: python app.py --no-gui outputs/OpenMembraneBuilder-xxxx/config.json

docs.title: ✏️ Editing configurations
docs.text:
You can modify config.json to:

  • Change protein files
  • Adjust membrane composition
  • Modify box size or number of systems

This enables fast iteration without reopening the GUI.

docs.title: 📦 Output
docs.text:
The CLI produces the same outputs as the GUI:

  • Project folder in outputs/
  • ZIP archive in downloads/
  • Full reproducibility via config.json

docs.title: Contributing to OpenMembraneBuilder
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder is an open-source community-driven platform focused on reproducible, extensible, and collaborative scientific workflows and infrastructure.

We welcome contributions from developers, researchers, testers, and designers.

docs.title: Ways to Contribute
docs.text: Contributions can broadly be divided into two categories:

docs.title: 1. Testing and Validation
docs.text:
Testing is a critical part of the project and includes:

  • bug reporting
  • workflow validation
  • benchmarking
  • documentation improvements
  • reproducibility checks
  • platform compatibility testing
  • usability feedback

Scientific software quality strongly depends on rigorous testing and validation from the community.

docs.title: 2. Module and Feature Development
docs.text:
We also welcome technical contributions such as:

  • new modules
  • workflow integrations
  • UI/UX improvements
  • API integrations
  • visualization components
  • documentation systems
  • deployment tooling

The project is designed to evolve modularly, and community-developed components are highly encouraged.

docs.title: Academic Contribution and Authorship
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder is developed with an open-science philosophy.

Major contributors to the project may be recognized through authorship in associated academic manuscripts and preprints, depending on the scope and significance of their contributions.

docs.title: Living Preprint Model
docs.text:
The project aims to maintain a continuously updated preprint accompanying major releases of the platform.

For each major release:

  • contributors may be acknowledged or included as co-authors
  • release-specific contributions may be documented
  • major technical and scientific advancements may be summarized

This creates a transparent and evolving record of community contributions.

docs.title: Future Journal Submission
docs.text:
As the platform matures and stabilizes, we plan to submit an associated manuscript to a peer-reviewed scientific journal (e.g. methods- or infrastructure-oriented journals).

The goal is to establish OpenMembraneBuilder as:

  • a robust scientific platform
  • a reproducible open framework
  • a sustainable community-driven infrastructure

docs.title: How to Get Involved
docs.text:
If you would like to contribute, collaborate, or discuss ideas, please contact us at:

dev@open-builder.com

Please include:

  • your background/interests
  • areas you would like to contribute to

docs.title: GUI Usage
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder can be launched using Streamlit:

streamlit run app.py

docs.title: 🧭 What you can configure
docs.text:
The GUI allows you to configure:

  • System type (membrane or membrane + protein)
  • Box size
  • Martini force field
  • Membrane composition
  • Solvation and salt molarity
  • Number of replicas (systems)
  • Protein input files
  • Protein placement and rotation

docs.title: 🚀 Build Process
docs.text:
Press the BUILD button to generate your systems.

This will create a project folder:

outputs/<project_name>/

and automatically generate a downloadable ZIP archive.

docs.title: 🧬 Protein Input Files
docs.text:
For protein-containing systems, upload:

  • A coarse-grained .pdb file
  • The corresponding .itp topology file

These files are copied into:

user_inputs/

inside the output project folder, ensuring the build is fully reproducible.

docs.title: 📦 Output Summary
docs.text:
After building, you will have:

  • A complete project folder inside outputs/
  • A ZIP archive in downloads/
  • All inputs and configuration stored for reuse

docs.title: Stable version
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/lolicato/OpenMembraneBuilder.git
cd OpenMembraneBuilder

docs.title: Development version (specific branch)
docs.text:
git clone -b development https://github.com/lolicato/OpenMembraneBuilder.git
cd OpenMembraneBuilder

docs.title: 🐍 Conda Environment
docs.text:
We recommend installing OpenMembraneBuilder using a Conda environment:

conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate OpenMembraneBuilder # activate OpenMembraneBuilder-dev for development version

docs.title: GUI mode
docs.text: streamlit run app.py

docs.title: CLI mode
docs.text: python app.py --no-gui outputs/OpenMembraneBuilder-xxxx/config.json

docs.title: 📦 Notes
docs.text:
• coby is used for system generation
  • MDAnalysis handles structure manipulation
  • streamlit provides the GUI
  • streamlit-molstar enables 3D visualization

docs.title: 🔧 Optional (Documentation)
docs.text:
If you want to build the documentation locally:

pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]"
mkdocs serve

docs.title: JSON Configuration
docs.text:
Each build writes a config.json file inside the output folder.

This file stores the full build configuration and allows full reproducibility of the system.

docs.title: 🧱 System
docs.text:
• selected_module
  • "membrane"

  • "membrane_with_cg_protein"

  • selected_ff

  • Force field (currently martini_v3)

docs.title: 📦 Box
docs.text:
• box_x, box_y, box_z → size in nm
  • box_type → currently "rectangular"

docs.title: 🧂 Solvation
docs.text:
• solvation → string passed to COBY
  • salt_molarity → numeric version (used internally)

docs.title: 🔁 Replicas
docs.text: • n_systems → number of independent systems generated

docs.title: 🧬 Protein
docs.text:
• pdb_path → protein structure
  • itp_path → topology

These are automatically copied into:

user_inputs/

docs.title: 📍 Placement
docs.text:
• z_method
  • "Absolute z position"

  • "Height above Membrane"

  • distance_to_mem

  • Used only for height-based placement

docs.title: 🎲 Randomization
docs.text:
• randomize_pos
  • randomize_pos_every
  • randomize_rot
  • randomize_rot_every

Controls variability across replicas.

docs.title: 🧬 Membrane Composition
docs.text:
Each lipid entry follows:

[lipid_name, upper, lower, apl_upper, apl_lower]

Example:

["POPC", 0.5, 1.0, 0.6, 0.6]

docs.title: Relative mode (abs_lip_vals = false)
docs.text: • Values must sum to 1.0 per leaflet

docs.title: Absolute mode (abs_lip_vals = true)
docs.text: • Values are lipid counts (integers)

docs.title: ⚠️ Notes
docs.text:
• membrane_string is generated automatically → do not edit
  • entries is an internal field
  • output_name is set automatically

docs.title: 🚀 Reuse
docs.text: python app.py --no-gui outputs/OpenMembraneBuilder-xxxx/config.json

docs.title: Membrane Templates
docs.text: OpenMembraneBuilder supports loading membrane compositions from CSV or OpenMembraneBuilder template (.ob) files. This feature allows users to quickly generate reproducible membrane systems and batch-create multiple membrane compositions from a single file.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
# ExampleMembrane1

;resname,upper_leaflet,lower_leaflet,apl_upper,apl_lower
POPC,0.60,0.40,0.61,0.61
DOPC,0.25,0.40,0.67,0.67
CHOL,0.15,0.20,0.40,0.40

# ExampleMembrane2

;resname,upper_leaflet,lower_leaflet,apl_upper,apl_lower
POPC,0.60,0.20,0.61,0.61
DOPC,0.25,0.20,0.67,0.67
CHOL,0.15,0.60,0.40,0.40

This example defines two asymmetric membranes composed of POPC, DOPC, and cholesterol.

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
A template consists of one or more membrane definitions.

Each membrane definition starts with a name line:

# MembraneName

The membrane name is used for:

  • Template identification
  • Replica folder naming
  • Output organization

If only a single membrane composition is required, the name line can be omitted and the file may be used as a standard CSV.

docs.title: Template Format
docs.text:
Lines starting with ; are treated as comments and ignored by OpenMembraneBuilder. Each lipid is defined on a separate line:

; resname,upper_leaflet,lower_leaflet,apl_upper,apl_lower

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description resname Lipid residue name upper_leaflet Ratio or count in the upper leaflet lower_leaflet Ratio or count in the lower leaflet apl_upper Area per lipid (nm²) in the upper leaflet apl_lower Area per lipid (nm²) in the lower leaflet

docs.title: Single Membrane Example
docs.text:
;resname,upper_leaflet,lower_leaflet,apl_upper,apl_lower
POPC,0.70,0.30,0.61,0.61
DOPC,0.30,0.70,,

Missing APL values automatically receive the default value of 0.60 nm².

docs.title: Multiple Membrane Definitions
docs.text:
A single file may contain multiple membrane compositions.

# PlasmaMembrane

;resname,upper_leaflet,lower_leaflet,apl_upper,apl_lower
POPC,0.70,0.30,0.61,0.61
DOPC,0.30,0.70,,

# CholesterolRich

;resname,upper_leaflet,lower_leaflet,apl_upper,apl_lower
POPC,0.50,0.40,0.61,0.61
CHOL,0.50,0.60,0.40,0.40

Each membrane will be processed independently.

docs.title: Area Per Lipid APL
docs.text:
APL controls membrane packing density.

APL Effect Smaller values Tighter packing Larger values Looser packing

If omitted:

POPC,0.70,0.30

or

POPC,0.70,0.30,,

OpenMembraneBuilder assigns 0.60 nm² automatically.

docs.title: Ratios and Absolute Counts
docs.text: Two composition modes are supported.

docs.title: Relative Ratios
docs.text:
POPC,0.70,0.30
DOPC,0.30,0.70

docs.title: Absolute Counts
docs.text:
POPC,70,30
DOPC,30,70

Warning

Do not mix ratios and absolute counts within the same membrane definition.

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder accepts:

  • .csv
  • .ob

Both formats use the same internal structure.

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text: OpenMembraneBuilder writes all builds into the outputs/ directory.

docs.title: 📁 Project Folder
docs.text:
Each build creates a self-contained project:

outputs/OpenMembraneBuilder-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS/
├── config.json
├── user_inputs/
├── simulations/
├── toppar/
└── mdp/

docs.title: 📄 config.json
docs.text:
Stores the full configuration used for the build.

  • Enables full reproducibility
  • Can be reused with CLI mode

docs.title: 🧬 user_inputs/
docs.text:
Contains all uploaded input files:

user_inputs/
├── protein.pdb
└── protein.itp

These files are copied automatically and included in the final ZIP.

docs.title: 🔁 simulations/
docs.text:
Contains one folder per replica:

simulations/
├── R0001/
├── R0002/
└── R0003/

Each folder includes:

  • generated system files
  • topology (topol.top)
  • simulation outputs (.gro, etc.)

docs.title: ⚛️ toppar/
docs.text:
Contains force field and topology files:

  • Martini force field files
  • protein topology (protein.itp)

docs.title: 🧪 mdp/
docs.text:
Contains simulation parameter files:

  • energy minimization (em.mdp)
  • equilibration (eq*.mdp)
  • production (md.mdp)

docs.title: 📦 ZIP Archive
docs.text:
A compressed copy of the entire project is automatically created:

downloads/OpenMembraneBuilder-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.zip

This archive includes everything needed to reproduce the system.

docs.title: ✅ Summary
docs.text:
Each build is:

  • Fully self-contained
  • Reproducible via config.json
  • Ready for simulation workflows
